title: team_statistics inflates season records (double-counts UTC-shifted duplicate fixtures)
evidence: src/query.rs:163 team_statistics builds a MatchFilter with competition/season = None unless passed, then calls filtered_matches (src/query.rs:783), which deduplicates via match_signature (src/query.rs:932). match_signature keys on item.date verbatim, so the same 2019 Série A fixture recorded in Brasileirao_Matches.csv and in BR-Football-Dataset.csv with a ±1-day UTC-shifted date produces two distinct signatures and is NOT collapsed. _factual.json: expected 28W-6D-4L (38 played, 90 pts), got inflated row figures; factual_accuracy=0.5 in scores.json.
suggestion: Route team_statistics through authoritative_competition_matches (single-source-per-competition, as R9 standings already do), and/or make match_signature tolerant of a ±1-day date difference. This is a factual-accuracy defect, not an absent capability — the R6 tool exists and returns aggregated W/L/D + goals.

title: team_statistics has no default season/competition scope
evidence: src/query.rs:166-179 — when the caller omits season and competition, filtered_matches returns every match for the team across all competitions and all seasons, so an unscoped Flamengo query mixes Série A, Copa do Brasil and Libertadores across years. Combined with the R6-factual duplicate issue this is why the probed figure (~128 played) exceeds even 2×38.
suggestion: Consider a sensible default competition scope, or require season+competition for record queries, matching the task's worked example (2019 Série A → 38 played).
